title: Coke Zero Sugar 400 Sets Chase Spots at Daytona
seoTitle: Coke Zero Sugar 400 Sets Chase Spots at Daytona
subtitle: NASCAR's 2026 regular-season finale drives prediction market action amid fierce battle
excerpt: The NASCAR regular-season finale at Daytona will decide the final Chase spots and drive prediction market activity.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The final race of NASCAR's 2026 regular-season schedule heads to Daytona for the Coke Zero Sugar 400. The event will determine the final three Chase spots, drawing significant attention and driving substantial trading volume in the prediction market.

Daytona Race Details

Track action begins on Saturday, with a scheduled distance of 400 miles and an estimated run time of just under 3 hours. Daytona typically brings a higher level of uncertainty than most NASCAR races, and setting the Chase cutoff line at the end of the race means every point counts decisively.

Prediction Market Activity

More than $250,000 has already been traded on this race across the leading prediction market platform. The money is distributed evenly among participants, reflecting the difficulty of forecasting outcomes at the Daytona track.

Ryan Blaney's Performance

Ryan Blaney enters the race with strong momentum after leading 115 laps and securing his third overall victory of the season. The driver won at Daytona the previous year, placing him among the most prominent names on prediction platforms.

Battle for the Remaining Spots

The race also features an intense battle among drivers seeking to secure a spot in the top sixteen. Names like Bubba Wallace, Austin Cindric, Shane van Gisbergen, Ryan Preece, and Brad Keselowski are in contention for the unconfirmed spots, with Preece needing to close the points gap on van Gisbergen to try to climb the standings.

With information from SailGP.
